Orchestration and session state must not depend on a single client staying connected for the duration of a workflow. Any multi-step, side-effecting sequence (e.g. push a branch, then create a task, then send the initial message) should be executed as a durable unit on the server/hub side rather than split across calls that assume the initiating client remains alive; if the client disconnects between steps, retries must not create duplicate side effects (e.g. re-pushing a new branch with a fresh attempt id) and must be able to detect/resume/clean up the partial state.

Likewise, when a run or session is already in progress, a new "start" request for the same id must reattach to the live run instead of silently replacing it (which would leave the old run unreachable with no abort and no queue, and would cause transcript writes to resolve against a stale snapshot). Similarly, signals/callbacks tied to a specific client connection should fail over to another connected participant that registered the same callback when the original owner disconnects, rather than immediately failing the run; only when no participant can service the callback should the run be treated as unrecoverable (and even then, document the limits, e.g. "does not guarantee recovery from a hub crash or machine restart").

Example pattern: instead of client code doing `push(); if (stillConnected) cloud.create()`, move the push+create+initial-send sequence into the durable layer so it completes atomically regardless of viewer connectivity, and add tests that simulate disconnect-during-run and callback-ownership handoff to another connected client.
